figures.name: Guru Nanak

ability.name: Ik Onkar
ability.description: All sectarian and divisive enemy abilities auto-fail; all allies gain +2 to all stats.

figures.description: The founder of Sikhism whose divine illumination revealed the One Creator beyond all religious divisions.

figures.name: Guru Gobind Singh

ability.name: Khalsa Power
ability.description: All Sikh warrior allies gain +4 power; create one Khalsa warrior ally with 7/7/7/7/7 stats.

figures.description: The tenth Guru who founded the Khalsa — the army of the pure — and composed the Dasam Granth's fierce mythology.

figures.name: Chandi

ability.name: Demon Slayer's Song
ability.description: Deal 6 damage to all dark enemies; Sikh warrior allies gain +3 power.

figures.description: The fierce warrior goddess of the Dasam Granth whose battles against demons Guru Gobind Singh immortalized in verse.

figures.name: Baba Deep Singh

ability.name: Severed Head Champion
ability.description: Even when this card's HP reaches 0, it acts for one final turn before falling.

figures.description: The legendary Sikh martyr who fought to the Golden Temple with his severed head held in his hand.

figures.name: Banda Singh Bahadur

ability.name: Liberation Charge
ability.description: Deal 5 damage to all enemies; free any ally who is immobilized or controlled.

figures.description: The fierce Sikh warrior leader who established the first Sikh sovereignty after Guru Gobind Singh.

figures.name: Guru Granth Sahib

ability.name: Eternal Shabad
ability.description: All allies gain +2 to all stats while the living scripture guides; enemy corruption abilities fail.

figures.description: The eternal living Guru of the Sikhs — the sacred scripture itself that contains all divine wisdom.

figures.name: Mata Sahib Kaur

ability.name: Mother of the Pure
ability.description: All Khalsa warriors gain +2 defense from the mother's blessing.

figures.description: The 'Mother of the Khalsa' who mixed sugar into the amrit ceremony creating the sweetness of divine grace.

figures.name: Ajit Singh

ability.name: Chamkaur Sacrifice
ability.description: When this card falls, all allies gain +3 power from the martyr's eternal strength.

figures.description: The eldest son of Guru Gobind Singh who died at the Battle of Chamkaur protecting the Sikh faith.

figures.name: Har Gobind

ability.name: Miri Piri
ability.description: This card wields temporal and spiritual power simultaneously: +2 power and +2 magic at all times.

figures.description: The sixth Guru who wielded two swords (miri and piri) representing temporal and spiritual authority united.

figures.name: Panj Pyare

ability.name: Five as One
ability.description: This card represents five: grant +1 to all five stats of any five different allies simultaneously.

figures.description: The Five Beloved — the first five volunteers who offered their heads to Guru Gobind Singh for the Khalsa.

figures.name: Waheguru

ability.name: Wonderful Lord
ability.description: All suffering effects on allies are negated; grant +3 magic to all who chant the divine name.

figures.description: The Sikh name for the divine — Waheguru — the Wondrous God whose name is the highest form of prayer.

figures.name: Ek Ong Kar

ability.name: One Creator
ability.description: All divisive or sectarian abilities used by enemies are redirected back at them.

figures.description: The opening affirmation of the Japji Sahib — One God, Creator of all — the foundation of Sikh theology.

figures.name: Guru Arjan Dev

ability.name: Martyr's Peace
ability.description: This card cannot be affected by torture, burning or pain abilities — grant +2 defense to all.

figures.description: The fifth Guru who compiled the Adi Granth and died under Mughal torture without uttering a word of complaint.

figures.name: Guru Tegh Bahadur

ability.name: Shield of Hind
ability.description: Absorb all damage targeting allies of other faiths for 1 turn.

figures.description: The ninth Guru who sacrificed himself to protect the religious freedom of Kashmiri Hindus from forced conversion.

figures.name: Bhai Ghanaya

ability.name: Universal Service
ability.description: Restore 2 HP to all cards on the field — including enemies — from the spirit of seva (service).

figures.description: The Sikh soldier who gave water to fallen enemies on the battlefield, earning Guru Gobind's praise.

figures.name: Nishan Sahib

ability.name: Khalsa Banner
ability.description: All Sikh and warrior allies gain +1 to all stats while the flag flies.

figures.description: The triangular blue banner of the Khalsa planted at every Gurdwara marking sovereign Sikh sacred space.

figures.name: Dastar

ability.name: Crown of Honor
ability.description: This card cannot be shamed, charmed or degraded by any enemy ability.

figures.description: The Sikh turban — the crown of honor that signifies sovereignty, courage and commitment to the Guru's path.

figures.name: Langar Spirit

ability.name: Langar Blessing
ability.description: Restore 1 HP to all allies every turn for 3 turns from the spirit of sharing.

figures.description: The spirit of the Sikh langar (free kitchen) where all — regardless of caste, creed or status — eat together.

figures.name: Mul Mantar

ability.name: Foundation Stone
ability.description: All enemy abilities that target the foundation of any ally's power auto-fail.

figures.description: The foundational verse of the Guru Granth Sahib that describes the divine nature in its essential truth.

figures.name: Jap Ji Sahib

ability.name: Morning Shabad
ability.description: All allies begin with +1 to all stats from the dawn prayer's blessing.

figures.description: The morning prayer composed by Guru Nanak that begins the Guru Granth Sahib and guides every Sikh day.
